name: browser/follow-docs
title: Find the exact docs
summary: Find the official documentation page for a library or tool, read the exact section and quote the command or API.
when: Use when the user needs the exact syntax of a command or API and a guess could be wrong.
steps: Call web_search with the library name plus official documentation and max_results 5, then ignore blog, forum and video results.
Call browser action open on the project's own domain, such as docs.python.org or doc.rust-lang.org, not a mirror or tutorial site.
Use the numbered link list from the browser result and call browser action open on the page whose title names your section.
Call browser action inspect with the url and a selector for the main content to read the exact paragraph and code block.
Copy the command or function signature character for character, with its arguments, and note the version the page shows.
Call run_command with python3 --version or npm --version to check the page's version against the one installed here.
If the site cannot be reached, say so plainly and quote a local manual page via run_command man or doc_search instead.
Give the quoted command, the page URL, the section heading and the version it applies to; never paraphrase a signature.
next: The final answer must contain the exact quoted command or signature, the documentation URL, the section and the version it applies to.
